text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak witnesses graduation ceremony at the police academy. Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi says security authorities will remain diligent watching out for terrorism until they uproot its satanic roots.
- Exports of Egypt's free zones increase by 23 percent in the first six months of 1997 to some $181.3 million, the State Authority for Investment said in a report.
- Diplomatic sources in Cairo told the state-owned Middle East News Agency that Mubarak would meet King Hussein of Jordan in Cairo within the few coming days.

- Alfi says contacts with Interpol are underway to get back millions of dollars from overseas accounts of Abdul Wahab el-Habbak. The former head of a state firm was recently sentenced to ten years in jail and ordered to pay 182 million pounds to the state.
- Mubarak received Libyan Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani yesterday. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa attended the meeting.
- Mubarak decides to raise salaries by 15 percent of those serving military conscription.

- An unknown wild beast attacks residents of a village north of Cairo. The beast, which resembles others that had attacked residents in rural and urban areas from the south to the north, bit four people and five animals. Residents managed to kill the dog-like beast.
- Egypt exports five million pounds worth of medicine to Iraq within the U.N. oil-for-food agreement.
